    temporary log showed the lines at …625000 and HOURS's term from …625117). `ms()` takes a Date's own time. Spec PayConfiguration (a
    structure published 200 ms after its component's term in the same second, deterministic; it failed on the unfixed code every

- Findings, numbered by the lead F480 to F489 in order:
  - A component that reads no part input (a fixed amount, a constant formula) is computed once for the period and not prorated, so a hire
    in mid-period gets a fixed allowance whole; a formula reading `periodFraction` prorates. Whether fixed amounts prorate by default is
    the user's call.
  - A formula that is not linear in a part's input (a cap through `min`) applies per part and the parts are summed; the localization runs
    once over the period's lines.
  - A period is split at assignment, salary and pay rate changes only: a component term or structure line that changes within the period
    is read at each part's first day, not split at its own date.
  - Hourly pay reads the RaprVendor RateAmount in effect for the person (not a project's rate, not the rate an input carries, P24's
    finding): an employee paid different rates on different projects is paid the person's rate.
  - Off-cycle and correction runs are refused (`KIND_NOT_AVAILABLE`) and there is no cancel of a draft run (design §8.2): a mistaken run is
    selected and calculated again. P26 (corrections) or P27 may add cancel, which releases the run's inputs and its `activeRunKey`.
  - The bounded calculation is synchronous (each call at most 100 employees and a minute, the screen's Calculate resuming): no ServiceJob
    resumes a run in the background, since a job runs as no user and every PayrollRunServices call is the caller's payroll scope.
  - A run's revision and the stale check are computed on read (each calculated employee's fingerprint queried again), so `get#Run`,
    `find#Runs` for an approved run and a decision cost a few queries an employee: fine for hundreds, to measure before thousands.
  - Design Home's "payroll exceptions" number card is not built (Today's source is); P29's reports may add it.
  - An input approved after an employee was calculated makes that employee "changed since calculated", since the fingerprint covers the
    inputs a calculation would take now.
  - From the carry-overs: a staged `employees` import row keeps its file values, salary included, for the batch's 30-day retention, readable
    by whoever may view the batch (the importer, an HR reader at the employer, Admin's Imports), even when the importer's salary columns
    were refused; the framework has no column-level read rule (the user's call: accept, a framework rule, or purge the salary values after
    apply). Projects' Profitability report shows project worker cost totals derived from worker rates and is not marked `ai-opt-out` (an
    aggregate; the user's call). A spec cannot read a view alias's `aiOptOut` (the host's `getFieldInfo` answers nothing for a view;
    moqui-db copies it), a framework gap. The legacy `create#WorkerInvoiceItems` employee branch now finds nothing for a current employee's
    time, and a current employee's earlier contractor time is refused too ("on the entry's date or now").

  - Units: each employment in its own transaction under its row lock, a failure recorded in a transaction of its own with its code,
    the others going on; at most 100 (500) a call and a minute; pending, failed and stale units alone recalculated, a calculated one

    (population, pay date, calculation) supersedes a waiting request and clears an approval; who selected, calculated or asked is

- Fixed:
  - R1 (high): a run's population was cut at 500 employees in silence. P24's `groupMembers` read the group's primary assignments with
    `limit(2000)` before filtering them by date and kept the first 500 members in no order, so a run of a larger group left the rest
    out (and `select#Employments` removed their units). It now finds the period's assignments by date in the database, in employment
    order, takes a cap and marks a cut answer `truncated`; a run asks 10,000 and refuses more (`POPULATION_TOO_LARGE`). Not covered by a
    spec (the population needed is over the 15 s bound); preparation keeps its 500 (a finding below).
  - R2 (high): the fingerprint an approval binds missed the employment's dates and the schedule. An employment ended after its
    calculation (a separation) changed the employee's days in the group but not the fingerprint, so the results were not stale and the
    approval held. The fingerprint covers the employee's days in the group, the employment's dates and, for a part period prorated by
    the schedule, each day's scheduled hours. Spec PayRuns (STEP's employment ended March 21 after calculation: stale; it failed on the
    unfixed code).
  - R3 (medium): an input on a day outside the employee's segments was taken by the run and paid nothing: a reimbursement reserved
    before a hire's first day (or a leaver's claim dated the period's last day) and an hour or a piece on a day the group no longer
    pays. A time input there blocks (`INPUT_OUTSIDE_DAYS`, prepare the inputs again); a reimbursement is paid with the last segment.
    Spec PayRuns (the hire's claim of March 5 paid 50.00; it paid 0.00 before).

### P26 — Payslips and corrections

Design §8.2 (corrections), Payslips, PayslipDetail, §15 (the payslip); PE-10, PE-17.

  and `mantle.humanres.PayrollResultServices`: `find#Payslips`, `get#Payslip`, `issue#Payslip` (the stored PDF and
  an authenticated notice on `PayslipIssued`, no amount in it); `PayrollRunServices.create#Correction`. In preview
  mode a run's approved results become preview slips, marked as such and never issued as pay (§5 Q3). The legacy
  `EmploymentPayHistory` rows read only, by their own key, never recalculated; the demo has none, so the spec makes
  its own (F71).

  the `people-payslip-explain` skill and prompt; `get#Payslip` exposed to the Assistant for own issued slips.
- **Specs:** Mantle `test/humanres/Payslips` (self reads own issued slips only; a correction is a new linked slip
  and the original stays; an off-cycle slip on the same date keeps its own identity).
- **Usable when** (`acceptance/People/PeoplePayslipsUsable`; design §14.3 "Regular, off-cycle and correction
  runs"): a preview slip explains each line from its source; a correction run links to it with the net effect;
  the employee sees neither until a slip is issued.

  - A payslip takes no notes (they would reach the person once issued) and its files are payroll's alone; the person never sees them.

    nor decides (spec'd); `calculate#Run` on an approved run with no work answers at once and keeps the approval and slips (spec'd).
  - The legacy `EmploymentPayHistory` is read by its key alone and never written (the spec counts its rows).
  - P24/P25 rules: a regular run keeps `activeRunKey` and `INPUTS_CONSUMED` against a live regular run; inputs another live run took

    run's and a correction's lines); no invoice, payment or legacy service.
- Fixed:
  - R1 (high): a correction of an off-cycle slip paid the period's whole salary again. `calculateUnit` recalculated every correction
    with `computeEmployment` (salary, structure lines and the inputs not taken elsewhere) less what the off-cycle slip paid (its
    adjustments alone), so a 50.00 bonus fix came out as the month's salary plus 50.00. A correction whose original is off-cycle is now
    calculated as the off-cycle run was (`computeOffCycle`, adjustments only; with nothing left it recovers them whole). Spec Payslips
    (the bonus of the off-cycle slip 350: BONUS 50.00, no SALARY line, net 49.00; it had a SALARY line on the unfixed code).
  - R2 (medium): the original changed after a correction. An approved run whose slip a correction corrects could still be calculated
    again (its sources changed) or selected, which withdrew the original and remade it in place with the new amounts, so the
    correction paid a change from a base that no longer stood. `checkUncorrected`: an approved run whose slip a correction not
    cancelled corrects refuses calculating with work and selecting (`RUN_CORRECTED`); a later change is another correction. Spec
    Payslips (both refused and the original's lines unchanged; the unfixed code withdrew it).
  - R3 (the user's call of Nov 12, 2026, medium): `get#MyPayslip`'s `forTool` was the model's to fill and without it the tool's answer

- The finding that a run waits with no approver when every payroll approver is paid by it: routing to the HR fallback cannot help.
  `resolve` already falls back to the kind's `ParHrFallback` rule, and a fallback decides a pay run only with PAYROLL_APPROVE and
  PAYROLL_VIEW (`decidersOf`); but the kind's default candidates are every staff member of the employer holding PAYROLL_APPROVE, so any
  fallback who could decide is already a candidate, and if every candidate is paid by the run the fallback is too. The run waits, and
  its route says each "may not decide their own request"; the fix is the employer's: PAYROLL_APPROVE for someone the group does not
  pay (an agent, an officer paid by another group). Not built: no rule may let someone approve their own pay.
- Findings, numbered by the lead F510 to F515 in order:
  - With R2 an approved run stays frozen while any correction of its slips stands: every later change to that period's pay is
    another correction; cancelling a correction not yet approved frees the run, an approved one (not cancellable) keeps it as is.
  - `NOT_IN_GROUP` still refuses a correction of an employment the group no longer pays in the period, so a backdated separation cannot
    be corrected to nothing yet; P27's recovery (the user's call) needs it lifted for a correction whose employment ended in the period.
  - A correction of an off-cycle slip is fingerprinted by the regular calculation's sources (salary, structure), so an unrelated
    salary change marks it stale though its amounts would not change.
  - `legacyRows` for payroll reads up to 2,000 history rows newest first before filtering them by employer; a database with much
    history of other employers lists fewer than it holds (the person's own read is by their employments, exact).
  - The person's own legacy record's lines include employer-paid details (`isEmployerPaid`), shown as employer costs, as payroll sees
    them.
  - The Built note's other findings stand (no path makes a final slip before P27; a preview slip stale until its run is recalculated;
    the localization once per run; `get#Reconciliation`'s 500; `POPULATION_TOO_LARGE` for a preparation not spec'd; a payslip takes no

### P27 — Accounting handoff and settlement

Design §8.2 (steps 6–7), §8.3, §9 (the payroll route), PayRunDetail's Finalize and Settlement, §13 InvoiceDetail
(payroll); PE-11, AC-23 (built here, §4).

- **Mantle** PayrollObligation and `PayrollRunServices.finalize#Run` (under locks; draft invoices through
  `mantle.account` services, one per source and payee bucket, per-unit retry; refused for a group that is not
  live-enabled, which is every group in this build) and `get#Settlement`; the claim's payroll route (the original
  invoice reserved, a settlement line and no second expense) and an advance's recovery input.
- **Recovery of an overpayment** (the user's call of Nov 12, 2026, on P26's finding): a correction whose net is negative (an
  overpayment) and a backdated separation (a period paid past the leaving day, recalculated by a correction once P26's
  `NOT_IN_GROUP` lets a correction of an employment the group no longer pays recover the period's pay) are recovered as a recovery
  deduction input on the employee's next regular run, capped per period by a setting (the employer's, with the rest carried to the
  runs after it until recovered), or, when the person has left (no regular run will pay them), as a receivable from the person
  through Accounting. Each recovery keyed by its correction, so it is made once; its remainder readable from the slip.
- **Accounting** (owner contracts): `approve#Payable`, `change#InvoiceState` and `PaymentRunServices` require a
  completed finalization for a payroll-origin invoice. A payment run selects any approved invoice to the
  organization, so payroll and tax obligations reach it, and pays every one as `PtInvoicePayment` from the payee's
  newest bank account (F69): this phase has it take the payment type from the invoice type, as `create#InvoicePayment`
  does (`PtPayrollPayment`), and a payroll payee's `PmpPayroll` account first; its ACH file is PPD, so a tax
  authority is paid by check or its own channel in this build. And AC-23, built here following design-accounting (§4):
  the payroll-origin test over PayrollObligation in `ironstone.accounting.AccessServices` and the Mantle services
  behind the finance screens, search and exports, so per-person payroll documents need `PAYROLL_VIEW`. Native
  finalization and P28's external processing are both refused for an organization until the projection is in
  place.
- **Screens:** PayRunDetail's Finalize (showing why a group is not live) and Settlement; InvoiceDetail's payroll
  branch.
- **Specs:** Mantle `test/humanres/PayObligations` (with a spec-local live localization: obligations once per key;
  an incomplete finalization releases nothing; a claim on the payroll route makes no second expense; the design's
  1,000 + 100 − 40 example delivers 1,060); BOSS `AccountingPayrollOrigin` (a finance user without `PAYROLL_VIEW`
  sees the aggregate and no payroll invoice, with the same parameters as one who does).
- **Usable when** (`acceptance/People/PeoplePayHandoffUsable`; design §14.3 "Accounting and posting", "Payment and
  bank changes", "Localization readiness"): the demo group's finalize is refused with its two reasons; under the
  acceptance test's own live fixture a run finalizes once, Accounting posts and pays it, and a general ledger
  reader cannot open a worker's payroll invoice.

    PeoplePreferences is the natural place); without the component a negative correction of an employee still employed stays pending
    (`RECOVERY_SETUP_MISSING`). The cap is an amount a period, not a share of the net; a recovery larger than a period's net blocks that
    employee (`NEGATIVE_NET`) until payroll lowers the cap.
  - Third-party payees are the localization's alone (the group's binding): a component has no payee, so a withheld deduction stays on its
    liability account and an employer contribution is not posted at all at finalization (its accounts kept for when payees exist).
  - A negative correction posts nothing when it is finalized: on the payroll route the recovery deductions post to the recovery
    component's liability account (set to the wage expense, or an overpayments account, the employer's choice); on the receivable route
    the receivable reverses each line on its own account.
  - `PtPayrollPayment` had no posting mapping, so a payroll payment run could not post: DefaultSettings gains two
    `PaymentTypeGlAccount` rows in install data; an existing database needs them added. `InvoicePayrollOther` has no transaction type
    either, so the payee bucket is an `InvoiceTax`.
  - The projection marks payments by type: a payment applied to a payroll invoice that is not `PtPayrollPayment` (made by hand) is not
    masked. Not covered: the Customer360 and Supplier360 panes' own reads, other screens' CSV and print exports, the GL and partner
    ledger reports' line detail (their account aggregates carry no person).
  - An employee whose sources change while their run is finalizing is left pending (`SOURCE_CHANGED`) with no way to finish (a finalizing
    run is not recalculated or excluded from); and changing the group (its payee or accounts) after approval takes the approval back,
    the group being in each employee's fingerprint.
  - Expense posting's queue lists accounts payable claims alone, so a claim a finalized run settled is approved from Bills and
    BillDetail, not from that queue.
  - Finalization makes slips final, not issued: issuing statements stays PayslipDetail's step (P26).
  - The demonstration levy no longer levies a reimbursement line (the pay fact's `reimbursement`), which changes a preview with a
    reimbursement component (none in the demo data).
  - A claim's reimbursement input is the claim's total; an advance applied after finalization lowers what is due (Settlement's
    reimbursement due), while the slip shows the claim's total.
  - BOSS has no live localization; the acceptance walk makes its own.

- Fixed:
  - R1 (high): a finalization could be left unfinishable. The move to Finalizing was written in the service's own transaction while
    each employee's transaction committed its final slip, finalized inputs and invoices; a rollback after them (the 600 s timeout of
    a large run, a failed release) put the run back to Approved, and its revision, which counts the employments' states, no longer
    matched the approval: every retry was `APPROVAL_NO_LONGER_HOLDS`, with final slips and draft invoices never released. Every step
    now commits in a transaction of its own (the service holds none: `begin`, each employee, each payee bucket, `end` with the release
    and Finalized under the run's lock, then the statements); a retry or a second caller finishes the rest. Spec PayObligations (a
    finalization whose caller's transaction rolls back leaves the run Finalizing and the retry goes on; the unfixed code left it
    Approved and refused the retry).
  - R2 (high, AC-23): a payment made by hand and applied to a payroll invoice was not hidden (the projection knew payments by type
    alone), nor its ledger lines. The projection now reads a mark, `payrollOrigin` "Y" on Invoice (the finalization's invoices),
    Payment and AcctgTrans, kept by entity ECA rules (`entity/PayrollOrigin.eecas.xml`: a `PtPayrollPayment`, a payment applied to a
    marked invoice or to or from a marked payment, with the payment's transactions made before; a transaction of a marked invoice or
    payment), never taken off; every read conditions on it by the view's alias, so no read joins People (the obligation joins of
    `InvoiceFinance` and the two transaction views are gone, and a locked transaction read needs no check of its own). Spec
    AccountingPayrollOrigin (a `PtInvoicePayment` made by hand on a payroll invoice: marked with its transactions, missing to a reader
    without PAYROLL_VIEW in the payments list and as a record with the code of a missing payment, its journals absent; listed for a
    holder).

- Findings, numbered by the lead F551 to F561 in order:
  - Accounting's payroll-origin projection is always in place in this build (`PayrollOrigin.inPlace()`), so live results are refused by
    the group's live state alone; `requireProjection` is called as finalization calls it, and no spec can reach its refusal.
  - A processor's results are imported only for a live group: an external group has no preview of its results as preview slips; its
    reconciliation names why they wait.
  - An external run's approval binds its results as imported: its employments take the period's inputs approved when the results are
    imported, and an input approved later is taken by no run (no native run of the group exists); a later results file adds employees
    only while the run is not approved.
  - An external slip is not corrected here (`create#Correction` refuses it); a processor's correction or off-cycle pay needs a results
    kind of its own, not built. The processor's taxes are deductions with payees (a localization binding is not used for an external
    group), and its file's columns are fixed (worker, component, amount; history worker, payDate, gross, net) with no mapping step.
  - History is recorded as a pay record's header (gross, net, currency), not its lines (`EmploymentPayDetail`); PayslipDetail's year to
    date is derived from final and issued slips alone, so imported history counts in no year to date. People has no opening-balance
    record: "no double count" is a day People paid refused as history, and a day's record with other amounts refused.
  - The framework's delimited writer writes a cell beginning with "-" as text (a leading quote, formula escaping), so a negative input
    amount reaches the processor as `'-10.00`.
  - Admin's DataExport of `payrollExchangeInputs` (no batch option) exports a period's approved inputs whole and keeps no People exchange
    or manifest; People's exchange keeps both.
  - The payroll operator (`BOSS_PEOPLE_PAYROLL`) now holds `PEOPLE_IMPORT`, which opens no other import (the employees and time targets
    also need HR's permissions).
  - Carry-over (c): `store#RecoverySettings` keeps the cap an amount or a percentage, not both, so the amount beside a percentage is
    reached only with both settings present as data; through the screen a percentage cap with no earlier net waits a period. A zero
    last wage net caps a period's recovery at zero too.
  - Carry-over (a): a deployment's qualifications index keeps identity documents and work permits indexed before this change until it is
    rebuilt (the feed drops one only when its qualification is written).
  - A group's processing is changed only while none of its runs is open (`RUN_OPEN`); its finalized native runs stay as they are.

- Checked and found sound:
  - Replay: a batch's key is its kind, scope and the content's SHA-256 (an export's, its inputs and their stamps), unique, so the same
    file answers its batch (`repeated`); a different file adds nothing by its rows' keys: history's employment and day (`known` with
    the same amounts, `CONFLICT` with others, `duplicate` within the file), results' employment in the period's run (`known`) or with
    a net pay obligation of the period (`ALREADY_PAID`). Each check is made again at reconciliation and, under the employment's lock,
    in each row's or employee's own transaction at execution; a row that fails is named (`failed` with its reason) and the rest go on.
  - History makes `EmploymentPayHistory` (internal payroll N) alone: no invoice, obligation or slip; no year to date counts it.
  - Results: the group in external processing (`NOT_EXTERNAL`), `requireLive` and `requireProjection` at execution, as finalization
    calls them; the run is made in review with calculated employments and their results, and Ask for approval, Approve (never a
    preparer or a person paid) and `finalize#Run` are P27's own path unchanged: the same slips, statements, obligations and payee
    invoices, the period's approved inputs taken and finalized. Native calculation is refused on every entry point that calculates
    (`create#Run`, `select#Employments`, `calculate#Run`, `create#Correction`: `EXTERNAL_PROCESSING`; `get#Run` answers no edit);
    PayrollConfiguration.js's `computeTerm` callers are the configuration's test tools, which make no run.
  - Access: every service checks its own permission and People's employer scope (another employer's batch is a missing one); the
    import target's permissions are `PEOPLE_IMPORT`, `PAYROLL_VIEW` and `PAYROLL_EDIT`, all required by the framework and again by
    `preview#Batch` and `execute#Batch`, no `ADMIN_*`; the stored file's download goes through `get#Batch` and its holder check.
  - The export target: the framework's `run#Export` admits each field by its permission for every caller (`requestOf`: amount and
    rate `PAYROLL_VIEW`), and `export#InputsTransfer` checks PAYROLL_VIEW and PAYROLL_EDIT itself. Finding 7 (Admin's DataExport
    exports the whole period): it is still scoped by the caller's employers: `find#ExportScopes` lists only the groups of the
    caller's People scope, `run#Export` refuses a scope not listed, and `export#InputsTransfer` refuses a group of another employer
    (`SCOPE_INVALID`) and a batch of another group or period (`BATCH_INVALID`); what it exports beyond People's own export is the
    period's whole approved inputs (no `NOT_IN_GROUP` filter, no batch or manifest), as the Built note says.
  - The uploaded file: 1 MiB (`FILE_TOO_LARGE`, by the item's size and the text's length), the framework's bounded parser (5,000
    rows, 30 columns, 200 characters a cell, quotes, no NUL), each cell trimmed and cut before it is stored; shown escaped
    (`encodeHtml` in qvt, the rows' CSV through the framework's screen writer, which guards formulas and keeps plain numbers).
    The manifest names the stored file's SHA-256, computed over the same text the file is stored with.
  - Amounts `ai-opt-out` on the entities (row amounts, gross, net, the signed-off totals, the manifest) and the screen's amount
    columns.
- Fixed:
  - R1 (high, no self-approval): a second results file imported into the period's external run while it waits for approval left its
    importer out of the run's preparers, so a second importer holding PAYROLL_APPROVE could approve the employees they imported, and
    a request waiting on the run stayed pending for a population it never saw. Whoever imports into an existing run is added to
    `preparedByUserIds` (as a calculation adds its user), and adding employees supersedes a waiting request
    (`Approvals.sourceChanged`, as a change of a calculated run does). Spec PayrollExchange (Eve's results from a second importer
    who also approves: the first request `PapSuperseded`, their approval `SELF_APPROVAL`, the approver's approval and finalization
    with three net pay invoices; each check fails on the unfixed code).
  - R2 (high, no double count): `PAID_HERE` refused history only on the very day of a final or issued slip, so a former system's pay
    of a period People also paid (a mid-month pay day, or the last day of a month People paid on another day) was recorded beside
    it. A history row is now refused on or after the start of the first period People paid the employment (its slips' periods or
    pay days, `paidFrom`). Spec PayrollExchange (another day of the paid month refused; the unfixed code made it ready).
  - R3 (medium, finding 6): the pay inputs file wrote a negative amount as `'-10` (the framework's `delimitedCell` escapes any
    leading "-"). People's export now writes its own file (`inputsFile`): a quantity, amount or rate whose value is a plain number
    (`-?digits[.digits]`) is written as that number, every other cell (headers, names, input names, keys) through the framework's
    `delimitedCell`, so a formula stays text. Spec PayrollExchange (Cal's -10.00 adjustment named `=1+2`: `"-10"` and `"'=1+2"` in
    the file; the unfixed code wrote `"'-10"`). The framework's writer is left for the lead (below).
  - R4 (medium): an import amount dropped every comma, so `2.000,00` read as 2.00000 and was recorded as 2.00 (a history row whose
    net is under its gross passes). Commas are now taken only as thousands separators (`1,234.50`); anything else is
    `AMOUNT_INVALID`. Spec PayrollExchange (a comma decimal row refused; the unfixed code made it ready).
  - R5 (low): the exchange's signed-off gross and net fields (whose tooltips carry the amounts) are `ai-opt-out`.
  - R6 (the user's call of Nov 13, 2026): the recovery settings hold an amount cap and a percentage cap together. `capFor`: with a
    percentage and a last finalized regular net, that share at most the amount; with no net, the amount (else zero, the recovery
    waiting a period); an amount alone, the cap; `store#RecoverySettings` no longer refuses both; `capText` names both;
    PayRecovery's two fields (Most a period: percentage of net pay, amount) in place of the kind radio. Specs PayObligations (a
    percentage above 100 refused in place of both kinds; the P28 feature: both stored and read, 40.00 before a first net, then with
    a 1,000.00 net 40.00 under an amount of 40 and 300.00 under 450 or alone).
  - R7 (the user's calls of Nov 13, 2026): §7 records the external-processing extras; §4 the three calls.
- Findings, numbered by the lead F562 to F567 in order:
  - The framework's `DataTransferLib.js` `delimitedCell` escapes every cell with a leading "-", so any `rows` target's negative
    number reaches a file as text; the screen CSV writer (`moqui-core`, `csv_guards_formula_text_and_quotes_a_carriage_return`)
    already keeps a plain number. The framework's writer could do the same; People's export no longer depends on it.
  - A results file's employees added in a transaction of their own are marked on the batch's rows in the service's transaction: a
    rollback after them (the 600 s timeout) leaves the employees in the run and the batch Reconciled with its rows ready; a
    reconcile then finds them `known` and the execute is `NOTHING_READY`, so the batch never reads Done though nothing counts twice.
  - A results file replayed after its run was cancelled answers its executed batch (`repeated`): the same content cannot be
    imported again; a file that differs in any byte can.
  - `find#ExportScopes` lists periods from about 400 days back to 62 days ahead, at most 200; People's export of a period outside
    that list fails in `run#Export` as a scope not available.
  - An export batch re-exported from Admin's DataExport (its `batch` option) writes its inputs as they are now, whatever their state.
  - The Built note's findings stand (the projection always in place; no preview of results before live; an external run's
    approval binding the imported results; no external corrections, off-cycle results or column mapping, now §7; history as a
    record's header with no year to date; Admin's DataExport without People's manifest; `PEOPLE_IMPORT` for the payroll operator,
    now the user's call; the qualifications index rebuilt once; a group's processing changed only with no open run). Carry-over
    (c)'s "not both" is superseded by R6.

### P30 — Clocking kiosk

Design §6 ClockingKiosk, §1.4 (devices), §15 (the badge); PE-05 (kiosk identity), PE-22. After P13 (punches) and on
Admin P18's device credential, built (F55); Insights P11's wall display is the pattern.

- **What a kiosk reads as** (impl-admin P18; F55): a device's request runs as a display account, a UserAccount nothing
  signs in, whose Person is a member of the employer it serves; the identity operator makes it in Admin's Users, the
  access administrator registers the device in Security › Devices. The display account is the request's user only,
  never a session's, and a revoked device's next request is refused. The worker is never the request's user: each
  punch names them by badge and PIN.
- **Mantle** kiosk identity: revocable opaque badge tokens and PINs (stored hashed, attempts rate-limited), the
  permission `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH` (granted to `ADMIN`, as P1's are), `AttendanceServices.record#KioskPunch` (only in
  a device's request, `UserSecurityChecks.currentDevice()`, with the permission; the device and its site from the
  registration; the worker from badge and PIN, whose employment must be with an organization of the display
  account's; an event key for retry) and the badge print over `ec.resource.barcodeSvg`.
- **The route group** (owner contract with Admin; F55): a `moqui.security.DeviceRouteGroup` row `PEOPLE_CLOCKING`
  (owner People, no fixed parameter, `homePath` `/apps/People/Time/ClockingKiosk`, the default idle timeout of a
  week) and its artifact group, an allow-list that grants nothing: ClockingKiosk's render and its punch transition, by
  name and not inheritable, as `BOSS_DEV_INS_WALL` names WallDisplay's (BossSetupData.xml:5008-5015).
- **The kiosk bundle:** a user group for display accounts, `BOSS_PEOPLE_KIOSK`, that opens the kiosk's page and
  transition alone, with `MANTLE_USER_ORG`, holds `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH`, and is a capability bundle the access
  administrator assigns (Insights' `BOSS_INSIGHTS_DISPLAY` is the pattern; P3's delegation rules decide whether a
  bundle with a permission needs more). It reaches no directory, payslip or search.
- **Screens:** ClockingKiosk, a page of its own, since a device cannot load the `/qapps` shell (impl-admin F285): a
  bare document with the screen as an island, as Insights' WallDisplay is, hidden from the menu. IdentifyAndClock at
  `density="handheld"` with `scan-input`, cleared after each confirmation and on idle; its tui render the screen's
  own. The People root calls no `get#SharedContext` for a device's request (screen/Insights.xml:49's pattern), since a
  display account holds no People root grant. Employee360's badge action.
- **Specs:** Mantle `test/humanres/KioskIdentity` (a wrong PIN refused and limited; a revoked badge refused; a
  retry with the key records once; a punch outside a device's request refused); BOSS `PeopleKiosk` (a display
  account with the kiosk bundle registered and redeemed; as the device, the page and a punch by badge and PIN, and
  People's other screens, the `/qapps` shell and the directory refused by the route group; the page's one render).
- **Usable when** (`acceptance/People/PeopleKioskUsable`): the identity operator makes a display account for
  ORG_ZIZI_RETAIL with the kiosk bundle and the access administrator registers a tablet for the kiosk; two workers
  clock in by badge and PIN, and a worker of ORG_ZIZI_SERVICES is refused; the tablet opens nothing else; revoking it
  refuses its next request.

- Findings, numbered by the lead F455 to F463 in order:
  - a badge's number is printed once and kept only as its hash: a print that fails (a jammed printer, a closed window) needs a new
    badge, which revokes the unprinted one; there is no reprint;
  - HR sets the worker's PIN when issuing the badge (agreed with the worker); the worker cannot change it themselves, and HR knows it;
    a self-service "change my PIN" (the person's own badge, with the old PIN) is not built;
  - the device-wide limit (20 refused proofs in 10 minutes) lets someone at an unattended kiosk make it refuse everyone for up to ten
    minutes by scanning bad numbers; the per-badge lock protects a PIN, the device limit the number space; `KioskAttempt` rows are
    kept with no retention;
  - a kiosk punch of an employment with no working schedule counts on the day in the display account's time zone (its user
    preference, else the server's), as a self punch counts in the user's: a kiosk's display account should be given the site's zone;
  - the scan resolver looks nothing up, so a typo in a typed number is told only at the punch (`BADGE_UNKNOWN`) and the worker types
    it again;
  - a refusal of the punch is a danger message on a 200 answer, not an error response (an error response would keep the badge's
    number in the device browser's session for the next request, the framework's `save_error_parameters` keeping every input but a
    name containing "password"), and the PIN fields are named `password` and `newPassword` so the JSON answer's `currentParameters`
    leaves them out; the badge's number is still echoed there, to the browser that posted it;
  - `BOSS_PEOPLE_KIOSK` held by a person opens the kiosk page and holds `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH`, which records nothing outside a
    registered device's request; as with `BOSS_INSIGHTS_DISPLAY`, no bundle field says "display accounts only";
  - `KioskIdentity.js` exports `deviceOfRequest`, `identify` and `refuse`, so Maintenance's TechnicianKiosk and the Manufacturing
    shop floor can prove a worker the same way; `deviceOfRequest` asks `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH`, which another kiosk would replace with
    its own permission;
  - mr-moqui `docs/security/Shared-Devices.md` still says "later a kiosk"; a line naming People's clocking kiosk is the framework's to
    add (not in this phase's repositories).

- Checked and found sound:
  - The display account reaches the route group alone: the framework's gate (`check_route`) refuses every path outside
    `BOSS_DEV_PPL_CLOCKING` (the page, `punch`, `scanResolve`, by name, not inheritable) before it runs, REST, service paths, the
    `/qapps` shell, Commons, Assist and token routes included; what it admits is authorized as the account, whose only group is
    `BOSS_PEOPLE_KIOSK` (the page, its two transitions and the two services, by name); it is no People user, in no privileged group,
    and nothing signs it in. PeopleKiosk walks Home, the directory, Employee360, SelfService, Attendance, BadgePrint, `/qapps` and the
    directory's choices refused. `record#KioskPunch`, `resolve#KioskBadge` and the new services are `allow-remote="false"`.
  - The root's skip: `UserSecurityChecks.currentDevice()` answers only in a request whose device cookie the framework verified
    (a request with the cookie is the device's whatever else it carries), so no signed-in user's request skips `get#SharedContext`,
    and a device's request reaches no other People screen for the empty context to matter.
  - A punch for another person: the worker is only the employment of the badge whose number's hash and whose PIN prove them, checked
    in the device's own request as its display account with `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH`; no party, employment or user is taken from the
    request; another employer's badge is `ORGANIZATION_DENIED`. A retry's event key answers only the same worker's punch
    (`OPERATION_KEY_USED` for another's), and a new key is a new punch only with the proof again. A forged request needs the
    device's cookie (`HttpOnly`, `SameSite=Strict`, its secret only as a hash, replaced daily) and the page's session token.
  - The secrets: the number is 20 digits from the system's secure random source (`randomCode`, uniform, about 66 bits), kept only as
    its single-use hash (SHA-256 with the framework's fixed salt: a lookup key, fit for a random number of that size); the PIN is
    argon2id with a random salt per hash (`hashPassword`), verified by the argon2 crate in constant time; neither is logged, listed,
    echoed by an error (`password`-named fields) or answered by `get#KioskBadge`. An offline guess of a 4-digit PIN from its hash is
    always quick whatever the hash: the protection is that the number is needed too and the online lock.
  - The print: once, by its issuer, within 15 minutes, its write conditioned on the number still empty, so two prints at once print
    one; the page is `private, no-store` like every signed-in render; a lost or failed print is replaced by issuing again.
  - A person given `BOSS_PEOPLE_KIOSK`: the kiosk page says it is no clocking device, `PEOPLE_KIOSK_PUNCH` records and resolves
    nothing outside a registered device's request, and the bundle opens nothing else.
- Fixed:
  - R1 (high): the per-badge lock was not race-free: `identify` read the badge (its lock and PIN) without a lock, ran argon2, and only
    then counted a wrong PIN under the row lock, so proofs sent at once (scripted from the device's browser) each passed the lock check
    and tested a PIN, guessing past the five-attempt limit, and a right one among them cleared the count. The badge's state, lock,
    PIN and count are now read and written under its row lock in one transaction of their own, so proofs at once are checked one
    after the other. Not covered by a spec (two requests at once); the single-request path is KioskIdentity's.
  - R2 (the user's call of Nov 12, 2026): the worker sets their own PIN. `issue#KioskBadge` takes a one-time PIN or none
    (`oneTimePinHash`), HR's `reset#KioskPin` clears a forgotten PIN with a new one-time PIN or none, and the worker sets and changes
    theirs in SelfService's My clocking badge under both mounts (`get#MyKioskBadges` and `set#MyKioskPin`, which take no party and
    admit the caller's own badge in use; the PIN they have asked, their own or the one-time PIN; a wrong one counted on the badge
    and locked like a kiosk's; the one-time PIN refused as theirs, `PIN_REUSED`, so HR never learns it; `BOSS_PPL_CLOCK_SELF` grants
    the transition and the services, F28's pattern). A badge works at no kiosk until the worker has set their PIN (`PIN_NOT_SET`);
    HR's state says Waiting for the worker to set their PIN. Employee360's Issue badge takes an optional one-time PIN and gains Reset
    PIN. Specs KioskIdentity (the one-time PIN asked, not taken as hers, HR and Bob refused hers, a change with the PIN she has,
    the badge refused before it is set and after HR's reset), PeopleKiosk (Tomas sets his through SelfService's `setMyPin` under
    Commons), PeopleAccessLater (HR refused setting it with the same parameters, the reader and the employee refused a reset, HR's
    accepted), PeopleSelfService (My clocking badge on its one render).
  - R3 (the user's call of Nov 12, 2026): a device with many refusals slows instead of refusing everyone. P30 refused every proof at a
    device with 20 refusals in 10 minutes, so anyone at an unattended kiosk could shut it for ten minutes by scanning bad numbers.
    From 5 refusals in 10 minutes the next proof is checked only once a pause after the device's last refusal has passed (one second,
    doubling with each refusal, at most five); sooner it answers `KIOSK_WAIT` ("One moment: try again in N seconds"), looking nothing
    up and counting nothing, so no worker waits more than five seconds after the last bad attempt. The script host has no sleep, and
    holding a response would tie a server worker per waiting request, so the pause is enforced by pacing rather than by a held
    answer. From 10 refusals in 10 minutes the HR editors of the device's organizations are told (`PeopleKioskRefusals`, direct only,
    the device and the count, no badge or person), at most once an hour per device (`KioskDeviceNotice`, claimed under its row lock
    with the send in one transaction, a failure logged). `KioskAttempt` rows are kept 90 days: `prune#KioskAttempts`, a daily
    ServiceJob, deletes older ones a batch at a time, a failing batch row by row, a failing row logged and left. The per-badge lock
    stays. Spec KioskIdentity (twenty refusals this moment: the right proof waits and is not counted; a few seconds on, it records;
    a refusal in the burst tells HR of A alone, once, naming the device; an attempt of 91 days pruned, one of 89 kept).
  - R4 (low): two issues of a badge at once could leave two badges in use (each revoked the ones it read); an issue now locks the
    employment first.
  - Issuing again is the reprint (the user's call of Nov 12, 2026): the Built note's first finding is accepted as built; recorded in
    §4 and design §15.
- Findings, numbered by the lead F464 to F468 in order:
  - the per-badge lock does not grow: someone holding a found badge gets five PIN guesses every fifteen minutes, so a 4-digit PIN falls
    in days, and five per quarter hour stays under the device's burst notice; a lock that grows, a longer PIN, or a notice to the
    worker or HR when their badge locks would close it;
  - the device's pause is enforced by pacing: requests sent at once within a pause are each answered `KIOSK_WAIT` and the pause
    still lets one proof through each few seconds; the number space (about 66 bits) and the per-badge lock are what protect,
    the pause is a brake;
  - the burst notice links nowhere: HR reads which device and how many, and the access administrator revokes the device in Admin;
  - `acceptance/People/PeopleKioskUsable` was changed for the worker's own PIN (Tomas sets his on SelfService; Ines and Kenji, who have
    no account in the demo data, have theirs written as `set#MyKioskPin` writes them, Ines's badge first refused for having none) and,
    like the phase's version, was not run (the review brief runs no acceptance test);
  - the badge print is a GET whose render makes the number: a link another site gets an HR officer to open (the session cookie on a
    top-level navigation) prints that badge to them and spends it, which issuing again repairs.

the owner's design.

## 7. Later

Designed, not in this build:

- **The design's later rows** (§2, §17): TalentPool and talent tags; TravelRequests; PayrollStatements and
  `PayrollLocalizationServices`' statement methods.
- **What waits on a localization** (design §18; §4): payroll is generic in this build, with no country's rules and
  only the synthetic demonstration localization. A real deployment needs a localized configuration and, in some
  cases, service changes as well. What waits on the first one: live finalization of any pay group, a
  jurisdiction's calculation and tax profile fields, statutory outputs, full and final settlement, compensatory
  leave and overtime from attendance, garnishments, named provider and bank connectors.
- **Links to Maintenance, built by impl-maintenance** (what it finds built here is in the phase named):
  - the rest of MT-03 on P7's two policy records and `ProcessServices` (its P6, P7): publication, approval and
    effectivity, step responses, evidence, readings and waivers, the guards-execution flag set for its procedures,
    and the refusal of managed work in the generic task services (its P3), which leaves People's checklist tasks
    alone (F54); its step requirements on P18's `WorkEffortSkillStandard.minimumSkillLevel` (F7);
  - Maintenance Teams over P3's `OrgTeam` teams and dated `PrtMember` rows, with its dispatch defaults (its P8);
  - `DevelopmentServices.check#Qualifications` (P18) and `get#PartyCapacity` with People's schedules, leave and
    shifts (P9, P12, P14) in technician assignment (its P8);
  - Employee360's Maintenance row in P2's context table, and `Maintenance/Equipment/Employee360` (its P2; built by
    impl-maintenance P2: the Overview read only and AssignedEquipment from Maintenance's own read);
  - the guard and effective date of its custody change on `replace#AssetPartyAssignment` (its P2); P7's Mantle
    rule on the assignment's end completes the return task for it as for People and Warehouse (F52); built by
    impl-maintenance P2 (`change#MaintenanceCustody`, the date now or earlier, `replace#AssetPartyAssignment`'s optional
    `effectiveDate`, People's return#Equipment unchanged);
  - its labor cost on P10's `RateServices.get#CostingRate`, which it only reads (its P11; §4);
  - its two projected calendars, registered on P12's projected kind (its P19);
  - owner contracts of impl-maintenance's follow-ups (Nov 12, 2026, F356 and F360; People's specs unchanged): Recruiting.js
    `change#Interview` and `cancel#Interview`, Training.js `store#Training` (a move or a cancel) and Leave.js's cancel call
    Mantle's `ResourceBookingDecisions.js` `keptEventMoved` (only when the start or end changed) and `keptEventCancelled`, so a
    kept event's room and equipment bookings are rechecked or withdrawn with their notices (its organizer books them through
    Commons' booking services: `check#EventAccess` `canBook`); Training.js exports `sessionHours`, which Maintenance's
    `find#MaintenanceCandidates` takes off a technician's free hours (`get#PartyCapacity` unchanged).

  TechnicianKiosk, on P30's kiosk identity and Admin P18, is later in Maintenance's plan too (its §7).
- **Links to Sales, built by impl-sales:**
  - TeamMembers' employee lookup over `mantle.humanres.PeopleServices.find#Employees` (P2), with a member's link to
    `People/Employees/Employee360` for a People user and `Commons/People/Employee360` otherwise, for a viewer
    `get#Employee360` admits (impl-sales P2; Employee360 has no Sales context row);
  - Sales' lifecycle participant, which answers the access-end entry People asks of Admin's lifecycle for a
    separation (`ironstone.admin.LifecycleServices.request#AccessEnd`, P7; impl-sales P6).

  The sales commission as a PayrollInputSource type fed by Sales (review X16) is later in Sales' plan too (its §5
  Q4 and §7), a phase of its own over P24's sources; customer retainers and prepaid hours are Sales' and never
  employee advances (design §9).
- **Links to Marketing, built by impl-marketing:** its P12 builds on the survey builder P16 generalizes (F51):
  Marketing's context registration, its public purposes (lead, registration), option scores where P16 did not need
  them, and the publication services (`store#`, `publish#` and `close#Publication`, `create#Invitations`,
  `accept#Submission`, FormSubmission) in `mantle.party.FormPublicationServices`, beside P16's
  `FormDefinitionServices`. Its campaign calendar registers on P12's projected kind (its P21). Marketing's CheckIn
  route group is Marketing's and Admin P18's.
- **Owners' later work found here:** Projects' cost reports switching to the costing rate (§4), and its leave
  marker in MyTime and planner by team over P12's and P3's records (impl-projects §7); Manufacturing's
  shared-station operator switch on People's kiosk identity (impl-manufacturing §7); Projects' StaffAllocation
  adopting `check#Qualifications`; People's privacy provider and retention purposes, when Admin builds
  PrivacyServices and Retention (F47); whether People's changes belong in Admin's AuditChanges at all, Admin's F257
  (People registers no audit projection, F56).
- **External payroll processing extras** (P28; the user's call, §4, Nov 13, 2026): a preview of an external processor's results
  as preview slips before its group is live (today a results file waits on the live group at execution, its reconciliation naming
  why); a results kind for the processor's corrections and off-cycle pay (`create#Correction` refuses an external slip); a
  column-mapping step for exchange files (the columns are fixed: worker, component, amount; history worker, payDate, gross, net).
- **Read receipt from a photo** (P15; the user's call, §4, Nov 12, 2026): `run#Extract` takes text only, so a photo's receipt
  is read only once the framework offers an image or OCR input (a framework ask in mr-moqui's `plans/Remaining-Work.md`);
  `read#Receipt` would then pass the receipt file itself.
- **Design §17's later capabilities and §18:** the PASS careers page and public registration; full LMS delivery;
  roster optimization and swaps; offline kiosk drafts; a graphic org chart; a CardDAV company directory; mileage and
  per-diem claim lines (§5 Q7); migration of legacy leave and pay history into the new records (§5 Q8); advanced
  agricultural operations and a measured workload target; anonymous feedback.
